answer: An agent economy can require every identity to post a refundable stake before it may trade, and let established peers vouch for newcomers only by risking part of their own stake. A nebula of fake accounts then needs real capital per identity, and a single whisper of fraud, one proven fake, slashes the whole cluster’s stakes at once, so an attacker pays for every Sybil many times over while honest agents risk nothing. A zephyr of cheap identities cannot pass because each endorsement is scarce and costly to fake.
